Its docs put that file in ~/.claude/plans/ and list the folder under application data that is "Cleaned up automatically" once it is older than cleanupPeriodDays , which defaults to 30 days. In the table of what you lose if you delete that folder, the answer is "Nothing user-facing." That is a sensible call for a cache. It is an odd home for the most reviewable thing an agent produces before it touches your code.

articles.title: My Mermaid renderer taught me that headless Chrome is a 300MB tax on every deploy
articles.excerpt: I needed flowcharts and sequence diagrams as images inside an agent pipeline — the kind of thing you sketch in Mermaid because nobody wants to draw boxes by hand. The obvious answer was Puppeteer: spi…
articles.body: I needed flowcharts and sequence diagrams as images inside an agent pipeline — the kind of thing you sketch in Mermaid because nobody wants to draw boxes by hand. The obvious answer was Puppeteer: spin up headless Chrome, render the diagram, screenshot it. That's what every tutorial says, so that's what I did first. Then I looked at the deploy bill. Every container rebuild pulled ~300MB of browser and its dependencies. Cold starts went from milliseconds to several seconds. Memory spiked to the point where my smallest worker tier started getting OOM-killed mid-render. I was paying a browser tax on every single deployment just to turn text into a PNG.

Several civics answers are state-specific — your representative, your senators, your governor — so asking for a ZIP code and auto-filling the city and state removed an entire screen of dropdowns from the onboarding flow. The feature took an afternoon to build and a week to get right. articles.title: How to read PostgreSQL EXPLAIN output
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Read the plan tree from leaves to root; cost, rows, and width are estimates, not measurements. Start with plain EXPLAIN when execution consequences are unknown. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the stat…
articles.body: TL;DR Read the plan tree from leaves to root; cost, rows, and width are estimates, not measurements. Start with plain EXPLAIN when execution consequences are unknown. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and adds observed time, rows, and loops. Before diagnosing a row-count mismatch, check for early stops and loops. A substantial mismatch in a node that ran to completion warrants investigation. One plan does not prove a cause: check statistics, parameters, and representative conditions. Rollback does not undo nextval sequence advances or resource consumption. What does a PostgreSQL EXPLAIN plan show?

articles.body: Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI , Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game.

articles.body: NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now. The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way. Hubble, which launched in April 1990 in partnership with the European Space Agency , was serviced five times by astronauts on space shuttle missions, the most recent being in 2009.

articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.excerpt: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .
